rivals.statement: Reach ceiling of the register. The autobench method stayed in the plain-prompt register (T 0.6, 4,096-token cap, 12-sample vote). A vote can only promote answers the register already reaches often. The terse plain register almost never solves the roughly 15 % of dev problems that need long deliberative reasoning, so its vote stops at its reach (about 84). The cue changes reach; voting only sharpens it. In a deliberative register, more samples keep adding problems whose per-sample rate is 0.2-0.5.
rivals.readers_wrong: The readers carried the cued base's vote gain (405 -> 446, and Wang's majority@k curve) over to the agent's plain-prompt vote, assuming voting closes the gap whatever the register. The plain T 0.6 register never reaches the deliberative problems, so 12 votes stop near 84.

holds_against.why: The plain prompt reaches the cue's score only when openings are selected (48.4 points from selection; control 216). The agent never selected openings, and at T 0.6 only about a third of plain answers open in the deliberative register, so its samples stay mostly terse.

Only 43 % of the cued base's vote failures have an agreeing wrong group; the rest are scattered or singleton. So failures are mostly reach and scatter, not locked wrong values, which is what this mechanism needs.

rivals.statement: Wrong-value attractors. At a fixed register and temperature, the base's wrong answers to a problem repeat one problem-specific wrong value instead of scattering. A majority vote therefore plateaus after a few samples at the share of problems where the right value is modal; extra samples add almost nothing. T 0.6 sharpens the attractors. The agent's 12-sample T 0.6 vote sat on that plateau (84, seeds 80-86); the cued base's vote nears its own plateau at 4 samples.
rivals.readers_wrong: The readers treated sample errors as independent (Condorcet-like), so they expected 12 votes to pass the 4-vote 89 % level. With correlated wrong values, made stronger by T 0.6, the vote plateaus early and lower.

holds_against.why: With only 4 samples, singleton ties dominate vote failures mechanically. As samples grow toward 12, the repeated wrong values become pluralities, so agreeing groups take over the failures; 43 % at k=4 already marks a large correlated share.

On hard328, 26 of 36 RL-vote wins have no right base sample (reach), but that compares the cued base with RL on the hardest problems. On dev100 MATH-500 problems right samples usually exist (cued pass@4 467), so the agent's shortfall there is selection by the vote, as claimed.
